clue.text: Not up-to-date concerning incorporating European region

indicators.note: incorporating means the first word takes the region into its middle

parts.note: anent is an old word meaning concerning or about
CI stands for the Channel Islands, a region of Europe

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a report about a corner of Europe is badly out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands (CI) are a British Crown dependency off the coast of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very old is by nature not current, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Major supporter sadly accepting closure of outfit

indicators.note: accepting means the exclamation takes the letter into its middle

parts.note: alas is an exclamation said sadly

indicators.note: the closure of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A key backer reluctantly agrees to shut down a company.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the Titan Atlas held up the heavens, the biggest supporting job there is.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titan who bore the sky on his shoulders is the archetypal great bearer of loads.

clue.text: Decorative work: studied endlessly, framing various oils

indicators.note: framing means the shortened word goes around the other letters
endlessly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to con a text is to study it closely

indicators.note: various means the letters of oils are put in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An art student pores over a decorated piece surrounded by assorted oil paints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts CONNED to CONNE, 'various' turns OILS into LOIS, and 'framing' puts LOIS inside CONNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloisonné is an enamelling technique in which colours are set in compartments of fine metal wire.

clue.text: Large-scale film downloaded to computer?

parts.note: E stands for electronic, as in e-book or e-mail
a pic is a film, short for picture

explanation.surface: A blockbuster movie is downloaded onto someone's laptop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large-scale film' looks like the whole definition, but only 'Large-scale' is; the film is the picture placed after the electronic E.
explanation.definitionFit: Something grand in scope or ambition, such as a heroic poem or vast undertaking, is described this way.

clue.text: Most of the people here will accept indecent music

indicators.note: will accept means the shortened word takes the other word into it
most of means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: these people here are these
blue means risqué or indecent, as in a blue joke

explanation.surface: Nearly everyone present will tolerate rude songs.
explanation.definitionFit: A melancholy African-American musical genre built on a twelve-bar pattern.

clue.text: Items on runway heading off arrivals at airport

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: planes landing at an airport are incoming flights

explanation.surface: An airport scene: things on the runway, with arriving planes peeling off.
explanation.definitionFit: A runway is edged and marked by rows of lamps that guide pilots in.

clue.text: Medical journal allowed to include an opening for chiropractor

indicators.note: to include means the word takes these letters into its middle

parts.note: to let is to allow

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A medical magazine is permitted to run a job advert for a chiropractor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lancet is a leading British medical journal, named after a surgical blade.

clue.text: Smug pair of heroes

indicators.note: a pair of means the word is written twice

parts.note: the heroes of a story are the goodies, one of whom is a goody

explanation.surface: Two heroes looking very pleased with themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone self-righteously virtuous is called by this term, an adjective as well as a noun.

clue.text: Response to drug preceding drug? Nonsense

indicators.note: preceding means the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: a trip is the hallucinatory experience a drug can cause
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea of a high leading to more drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe, literally stomach lining, is slang for rubbish or nonsense.

clue.text: Shift position as a result of being around large weapon

indicators.note: being around means the word goes round the letter

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly
on can mean as a result of, as in acting on advice

explanation.surface: Someone moves aside because a big person is nearby with a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy club used to beat someone is this kind of weapon.

clue.text: Variety of i.e. a cold one? Neither hot nor cold

indicators.note: a variety of something is a different form of it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, without the stops
taken as written
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about some kind of cold thing, answered with a lukewarm verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: The Laodicean church is condemned in Revelation for being lukewarm, neither hot nor cold, so the word came to mean half-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes someone lukewarm or half-hearted, from the biblical rebuke to the church at Laodicea.

clue.text: Love upset, relegating lecturer in college

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: relegating sends something down to the bottom, so the lecturer's letter is moved to the end

parts.note: to upset someone is to rile them

explanation.surface: A romance goes sour when a don is demoted within his college.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriel is one of the colleges of Oxford University.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel is the name of an Oxford college, so it is an instance of the general word.

clue.text: Section remains in band

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Part of something left over is found in a musical group.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a long strip of cloth worn round the waist or over the shoulder.

clue.text: Delay sheep jumping — I won't need them!

indicators.note: sheep jumping fences is the picture, and jumping letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: An insomniac puts off counting jumping sheep, while someone drowsy says they need none.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the drowsy person's own remark: someone already half asleep does not need to count sheep to drop off.
explanation.definitionFit: A drowsy person needs no sheep-counting to fall asleep, so this exclamation is what such a person would say.

clue.text: Artist leaving musicians in the German town

indicators.note: in means the shortened word goes inside the article

parts.note: der is a German word for the

indicators.note: leaving means those letters are taken out

parts.note: an orchestra is a body of musicians
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter walks out on a German band.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorchester is the county town of Dorset in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorchester is an English county town, so it is an example of the general word.

clue.text: Leader of gangsters stabbing solitary type resident in city

indicators.note: stabbing means the boss's word is driven into the middle of the other word

parts.note: a loner is someone who keeps to themselves
a Mafia boss is called a don

explanation.surface: A crime boss knifes a recluse who lives in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who lives in the British capital is called by this demonym.

clue.text: Legislator to look narrowly after long sentence

indicators.note: after means the looking word follows the sentence word

parts.note: a life sentence is the longest prison term
to peer is to look closely, squinting

explanation.surface: A lawmaker squints after a long prison term is passed.
explanation.walkthrough: A life peer sits in the British House of Lords for life, but the title is not inherited.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the House of Lords who helps make law, holding a non-hereditary title.

clue.text: Historical knowledge about invisible radiation in gallery

indicators.note: about means the knowledge word wraps around the radiation letters

parts.note: lore is traditional knowledge handed down
UV is ultraviolet, radiation beyond the visible spectrum

explanation.surface: Old learning about unseen rays is on display in an art museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louvre in Paris is one of the world's best-known art museums.

clue.text: Lover getting entangled with Mini, becoming scarlet

indicators.note: getting entangled means the letters are knotted together into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lover's tangle with a small car leaves them red in the face.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mini is a small British car.
explanation.definitionFit: Vermilion is a brilliant red pigment, close to scarlet in shade.

clue.text: Feeling unwell about employment? Show some sense about that

indicators.note: about here means the sense word goes around what came before

parts.note: nous is common sense
a is an abbreviation of about, used before dates
use is employment, as in putting something to use

explanation.surface: Someone feeling sick at the thought of work is told to be sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' appears twice: the first gives the letter A, the second wraps NOUS round AUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being queasy or sick to the stomach is the core sense of the word.

clue.text: Fiercer European clash disheartened European people

indicators.note: disheartened means each of the three words loses its heart, keeping only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A fiercer clash in Europe leaves its people dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator works on three words: Fiercer, European and clash each lose all but their outside letters, giving FR, EN and CH.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation of France's inhabitants are collectively called by this name.

clue.text: Make-up of marine tailless duck breed

indicators.note: the make-up of something is how its parts are arranged, so these letters are reassembled
tailless means both words lose their final letters

parts.note: taken as written before it loses its tail
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, and nada is Spanish-derived slang for nothing

explanation.surface: A puzzled look at the build of a sea creature and a stumpy breed of duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' docks both MARINE and NADA, leaving MARIN and NAD, which 'Make-up of' rearranges. 'duck breed' looks like the definition, but duck is the cricket score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a breed of duck, and also a variety of small orange, so it names a breed or variety.

clue.text: Luminance in difficult situations dazzles

indicators.note: in means the symbol goes inside the other word

parts.note: binds are awkward predicaments
L is the symbol for luminance

explanation.surface: Bright light in awkward moments leaves someone dazzled.
explanation.definitionFit: Bright light can make one temporarily unable to see, so to dazzle is to deprive of sight.

clue.text: Chap's last "nightcap" is something readily seen through

indicators.note: the last of the word Chap is its final letter

parts.note: a nightcap is a drink taken late at night, playfully a late glass

explanation.surface: A man's final drink before bed is described as transparent.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks flag that nightcap is being read loosely: a nightcap is literally a late glass of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Large sheets of clear glass used for shop windows are made to be looked through.

clue.text: No longer is embraced by a husband — extremely tearful?

indicators.note: embraced by means the past-tense word sits inside the other letters

parts.note: was is the past form of is, what no longer is

explanation.surface: A widow weeps, her husband's embrace a thing of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful definition: someone flooded with tears is figuratively swamped.
explanation.definitionFit: Awash means flooded with water, so a person in floods of tears is figuratively this.

clue.text: Central region about to be discounted in playing area

indicators.note: to be discounted means this letter is taken away

parts.note: a sports field is a pitch
c, for circa, means about

explanation.surface: The middle of a sports field is about to be marked down in price.
explanation.definitionFit: The core or heart of something, as in the pith of an argument.

clue.text: Stink over documents? Close

indicators.note: over in a down clue means the first word sits above the second

parts.note: hum is slang for a bad smell
ID is identity documents

explanation.surface: A bad smell rises over paperwork, and someone says to shut it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' is the muggy-weather adjective, not the verb to shut.
explanation.definitionFit: Close weather is warm, damp and airless, which is the same thing as muggy.

clue.text: Drink something between espresso and daiquiri?

definitions.text: Drink something between espresso and daiquiri?

parts.words: Drink something between espresso and daiquiri?
parts.note: a fizzy soft drink is what one might sip between a strong coffee and a rum cocktail, and its letters also bridge the end of the coffee and the start of the cocktail

explanation.surface: What would one drink between a coffee and a cocktail?
explanation.walkthrough: As well as the straight reading, the last two letters of espresso and the first two of daiquiri, read together, spell the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A fizzy mixer is a natural soft drink to have between coffee and an evening cocktail.

clue.text: Nice times with Australian, involved in swimming etc

indicators.note: involved in means these letters are put inside the other group
swimming means the letters of etc move about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
x is the multiplication sign for times

explanation.surface: An Australian visiting the French Riviera spends time swimming and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' turns ETC into ECT, and 'involved in' puts XA inside it. 'Nice' looks like the French resort, but it means precise.
explanation.definitionFit: Nice in its older sense means precise or finely judged, as in a nice distinction.

clue.text: New concoction of some lingo?

indicators.note: a new concoction is a fresh mixture, so the letters that follow are stirred into a different order

explanation.surface: Is this freshly invented word just a bit of jargon?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: mixing up SOME LINGO makes the word, and the clue read straight describes one, a newly made-up piece of language.
explanation.definitionFit: A newly coined word or expression is a fresh invention in language.

clue.text: Difficult work cut down when given to American singers

indicators.note: cut down means the word is shortened by losing its last letter

parts.note: a chore is a tiresome task
US stands for United States, so American

explanation.surface: A hard job is reduced in size once handed to an American.
explanation.definitionFit: A group singing together, as in an opera or church, is a chorus.

clue.text: Religious figure revived idea about new description of light in church?

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for saint

indicators.note: about means the reworked letters go around the single letter
revived means the letters of idea are given new life in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A saint comes up with a fresh idea about something new.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revived' turns IDEA into AIED, and 'about' wraps it round N to make AINED. The light is a window, not illumination.
explanation.definitionFit: Church windows are often made of coloured glass, described with this adjective.
